```markdown
# SEC filing ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 in the existing four-package uv workspace (repository scaffold).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second (SEC full-index and daily-index directories); measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks for the full history at 3 requests/second (index row count × request rate); not yet measured, measured by Stage 2 |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until submissions are on disk; measured by Stage 3 |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Index files to one table
      Objective: Download the real quarterly and daily index files and load them into one filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a filing-index table on disk, one row per index entry with its archive path; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: the table holds every quarterly index since 1993 plus the daily indexes since the last closed quarter, with its row count reported; the findings file records the run's wall time, request count and bytes downloaded
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability → Stage 4; point-in-time awareness → Stage 5; full validation suite → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submissions download
      Objective: Download the individual submissions that the index table's rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: the filing-index table and the measured request cost (Stage 1)
      Produces: submissions on disk, addressable by index row, with failed and pending downloads listed
      Exit: for a range named in the stage's spec, every submission the table lists is on disk or listed as failed or pending, and an interrupted run resumes without re-downloading completed files; the measured rate and bytes per submission are recorded
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability → Stage 4; full validation suite → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: submissions on disk addressable by index row (Stage 2)
      Produces: the main document of each 10-K and 8-K in Stage 2's range, extracted and linked to its index row
      Exit: every 10-K and 8-K in that range has its main document extracted or is listed with the reason it was not; the run's time and output volume are recorded
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability → Stage 4; full validation suite → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Manifests and traceability
      Objective: Add manifests and traceability across indexes, submissions and extracted documents, so stored inputs replay without new downloads.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: the outputs of Stages 1–3
      Produces: a manifest recording each stored file's source URL, received time and SHA-256, and each output's inputs
      Exit: every stored file and output traces to its source and hash, and rebuilding the Stage 1 table and Stage 3 extractions from stored files makes no SEC requests
      Leaves out: point-in-time awareness → Stage 5; full validation suite → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Point-in-time awareness
      Objective: Add point-in-time awareness to the filing-index table, so re-fetched quarterly indexes produce new versions rather than overwriting.
      Outcomes: O1 (hardening)
      Consumes: the manifest and hashes (Stage 4)
      Produces: versioned filing-index table, each version with its added, changed and removed rows
      Exit: a re-fetched quarterly index that differs from the stored one yields a new version listing its changes, the prior version stays readable, and no row is removed without explicit approval
      Leaves out: full validation suite → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full validation suite
      Objective: Add the full validation suite over indexes, submissions and extraction, run in CI on committed fixtures.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: the outputs of Stages 1–5
      Produces: committed fixtures and a CI suite that needs no SEC access
      Exit: CI passes offline on fixtures covering the historical index formats in the supported range, malformed and HTML-error responses, and the resume and versioning behaviour of Stages 2 and 5
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Add scheduling and deployment, so daily indexes, new submissions and quarterly re-fetches run unattended on a chosen platform.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening)
      Consumes: the validated pipeline (Stage 6)
      Produces: a deployed, scheduled pipeline with run reports and alerts
      Exit: scheduled daily runs are observed ingesting new index files and submissions, a missed run is caught up on the next one, and the weekly quarterly re-fetch runs on schedule
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

Retire only after a conformance audit (derive-roadmap §6) over O1–O3, with evidence per verdict: implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred_items entries. Unmet outcomes leave by a new stage or a written deferral.
```
